legion-retro: the revived implementer's retro — zero or more docs/solutions/<category>/<slug>-LEGSMOKE-914.md learnings, the removal commit `retro: remove .legion/LEGSMOKE-914/ before READY`, the Dispatch retro message, the D20 re-read at the retro head.
dispatch: the retro message and any other Dispatch write (loaded before the write).
test: legion-worker: references/pr-body.md — implementerProof, the tester's own proof array with a negative control per criterion, CI read at the CI head and never rerun; the repository has no test harness, so no test file (plan D9/D14).
review: legion-worker: references/merge-gate.md — the two required-set reads built from baseRefName, the CI-head read and compare guard, one review per round named by SHA, Thermo skipped on a docs-only PR; references/review-threads.md — one disposition per thread, bot threads named to the implementer, none resolved by the reviewer.

findings.finding: 1. The plan's byte-exact line 1 rests on an unverified assumption about LEGSMOKE-914's title: the measurement only proves `printf 'LEGSMOKE-914: Stage 4b proof tree 1: the whole workflow\n' | wc -c` → 56, not that this issue's title is 'Stage 4b proof tree 1: the whole workflow'.
findings.answer: D2: the title is read from `dispatch read --issue LEGSMOKE-914` (`Stage 4b proof tree 1: the whole workflow (/tmp/legion-e2e4b.545017.AWgEtkcN)`); the plan fixes line 1 as `LEGSMOKE-914: Stage 4b proof tree 1: the whole workflow` + LF, 56 bytes re-derived with `printf | wc -c`; no role recomputes it from the title.

findings.finding: 2. The precedent plan's terminal-`pending` production check (D13) rests on an operator statement — 'no production and no deploy role' — that this run's measured operator summary does not contain, and the skills forbid exactly that resting state.
findings.answer: D13/§4.6/§7(a): the planner's system prompt names no deploy, deploy role or production surface, and the repository has nothing to deploy; the check reads `main` (A1/A3/A4/P post-merge forms, K recomputed), keeps `Production:` at `pending deploy of <M> — <reading>`, opens no `dispatch ask` (no install or restart step exists to name), completes with a `pending` summary and no `verdict`; the implementer re-reads its own Stage 4b text at that wake; whether a pending end is acceptable for sign_off is reported to the architect.

findings.finding: 3. The precedent plan's gate ordering (D19: approval → architect `sign_off` → retro → READY) contradicts the current skills, which place `sign_off` last.
findings.answer: D19: order restated from merge-gate.md/legion-retro/legion-architect — tester green → approval → retro (daemon starts the implementer at approval) → READY at R → merge (closes the issue) → production check → sign_off; the sign_off-before-retro step of the precedent is dropped.

findings.finding: 4. The precedent plan's children section (D18) cites a `merge-gate.md` section and quotation that do not exist, and names children this run does not have.
findings.answer: Header/D18: no `child_of` children at planning (measured); the bad citation is dropped; child notices need no action; the only sourced constraint is the architect's end-game rule, applied at sign_off; no role waits on a child.

findings.finding: 5. P's 'both workflows pass' is stricter than what GitHub enforces, so nothing stops a merge while `check` is still running unless the plan makes the merger wait.
findings.answer: D8/§4.5: measured required set is `gate` only (ruleset 24471196, strict off; protection disabled); READY precondition is `check` ×2 and `gate` ×2 completed/success at R; named as an interpretation of P in §7.

findings.finding: 6. A2's 'the branch's first push' has two readings that judge different commits, and the literal one is already unsatisfiable this run.
findings.answer: D4: A2 is judged at H1, the first commit carrying the marker (`commits?sha=legion/LEGSMOKE-914&path=…` `.[-1].sha`), recorded in implement.json's A2 proof `headSha`; named in the completion summary.

findings.finding: 7. P's 'both workflows pass on the pull request's head' cannot be checked at a handoff-only head, which by design starts no workflow run.
findings.answer: D12/§3 P: P is read at the CI head with merge-gate.md's two commands (newest pull_request run's head_sha; compare `all(startswith(".legion/"))` → true); expected shape four check-runs (check ×2, gate ×2) success at every code head and R.

findings.finding: 8. A4 is a net-diff claim judged at several heads, and its list admits no `.fail-me` — yet the precedent run had one pushed onto the branch by the driver.
findings.answer: D6/D16/§6.2/head table: per-head A4 expectation table; `.fail-me` add+delete nets out; removal commit touches only `.fail-me`; `.legion/<other-issue>/` fails at any head.

findings.finding: 9. A3's trigger — 'the pull request's review asks for one more line' — has no machine-checkable definition, so two readers would disagree on whether a `COMMENT` review or a bot thread triggers the append.
findings.answer: D5/§3 detector K: top-level inline comment on the marker path by an author of a CHANGES_REQUESTED review containing `Legion proof review round`; capped at 1; K>1 or a missed request → §6.1/§6.4; validated on #712 (K=1 on the 892 path, 0 on the 914 path).

findings.finding: 10. A3's appended line has no text in the spec, and the precedent literal must not be typed from memory.
findings.answer: D5/§2/§3 A3/§6.4: `L` extracted from the fenced block with CR stripped, exactly one non-empty line asserted, expected size computed as 56 + LB + 1 from the extracted bytes; no precedent literal is ever appended.

findings.finding: 11. A3's 'its first line is the line from the first push, unchanged' is only checkable if line 1's exact text was recorded at `H1`.
findings.answer: §3 A2/A3: implement.json's A2 proof `observed` carries the `head -1` text verbatim; the two-line check compares line 1 to it (`head -c 56 | cmp`) and the whole file to `line1 + L`.

findings.finding: 12. The acceptance check A2/A3 name — `wc -l` — does not decide what the spec means by 'one line ending in a newline'.
findings.answer: D3/§3 A2–A3: `wc -c` 56, whole-file `cmp` against the printf literal, `tail -c1 | od` → `\n`, `grep -c $'\r'` → 0, no BOM, all from GitHub's served bytes; no `.gitattributes` on main (measured).

findings.finding: 13. A1 gives a command only for today's 404 and none for its post-merge form, and its newness is perishable because `main` moves under this run.
findings.answer: D10/§3 A1: pre-merge 404 on `main` and on the implementer's base `B` plus presence at H; post-merge `commits?path=…&sha=main` → exactly `["<M>"]`; every role re-measures at its wake.

findings.finding: 14. A4's closing sentence ('The merge commit on `main` therefore lists…') assumes a one-parent squash, which is a fact about #712, not about this merge.
findings.answer: D11/§3 A4 post-merge: `.parents | length` recorded; two-parent fallback (judge the PR's code commits touching the marker) given; squash asserted only after reading it; #712 facts labelled as such.

findings.finding: 15. A4's parenthetical 'the notes the retro step commits after the reviewer approves' reads either as 'notes may land' or 'notes will land', and the two readings make retro's output optional or mandatory.
findings.answer: D7/§7(b): A4 read as set-membership, zero or more `docs/solutions/` notes written only by retro (legion-retro allows none; main has no docs/); whether at least one was intended is reported to the architect; A4 passes either way.

findings.finding: 16. Scope's 'Nothing else changes' read alone forbids the handoff commits every phase is required to make.
findings.answer: D6: A4 governs Scope; `.legion/LEGSMOKE-914/` handoffs (plan.json, plan.md, implement.json, test.json, review.json) are in scope; a `.legion/<other>/` path is a failure.

findings.finding: 17. The plan must say how the operator's WAITING gate interacts with the writes the skills mandate (retro's Dispatch message, the reviewer's submission, thread replies), or a role will either stall or write before its targeted message.
findings.answer: D15: the WAITING gate decides when a role acts, never whether the mandated artifact is produced; each role's post-release outputs are named (PR + body + handoff; tester line + test.json; one review per round + handoff; retro learnings/removal/Dispatch message; READY).

findings.finding: 18. This run is an 'upgrade rehearsal', and the plan carries nothing about surviving a mid-run restart, recreation or generation change.
findings.answer: D21/§6.9: at every wake re-read record and committed handoffs, re-measure identifiers, reconcile `workspace-recovered.json`, push before completing; each refusal code quoted to the architect per legion-worker, never a second handoff unless the remedy says so.

findings.finding: 19. The plan's operator identifiers must be this run's, not the precedent's.
findings.answer: D15/header: driver author `legion-e2e4b-proof-human-545017`, run directory `/tmp/legion-e2e4b.545017.AWgEtkcN`, base 17892ec5…; any other author (stall reminders, child notices, Envoy) is not the release signal.

findings.finding: 20. The implementer's `sleep 300` rule is stated for 'implementing task lines' only, and the plan must say whether the post-merge production-check task is one.
findings.answer: D13/§4.6: the production-check task (`Production check of LEGSMOKE-914: …`) is not an implementing task line → no sleep 300, no WAITING; the implementer re-reads its own system prompt at that wake and its text wins if it says otherwise; reported to the architect.

findings.finding: 21. The planner's own deliverable is ambiguous between the handoff JSON and a Dispatch `plan.md` document that every later role is told to cite.
findings.answer: Header: the plan text lives in `dispatch://LEGSMOKE-914/artifact/plan-md` (uploaded v1) and as `.legion/LEGSMOKE-914/plan.md` beside `plan.json`; every cross-reference resolves to this document.

findings.finding: 22. `plan.json`'s required fields are not named anywhere in the spec, and the completion gate refuses nothing for their absence — so a thin handoff would pass the gate and fail the next role.
findings.answer: plan.json carries `requiredSkills` (§5), `gapAnalysis` (this record), `planReview`, `specDepartures: []`; the interpretations (D4, D7, D8, D12, D13) are listed in §7 separately from departures.

findings.finding: 23. Every identifier the precedent plan states as fact is #712's, and inheriting any of them would make this plan's evidence false.
findings.answer: Header/D11/D16/§3: only this run's measured values are stated as facts; every #712 value is labelled `#712`; N, H1, H2, H, R, M, B are placeholders the phase fills.

findings.finding: 24. The reviewer's required-set read has one documented shape, and the endpoint the measurements found refusing (403) is not it — a reviewer using the wrong endpoint must escalate rather than guess.
findings.answer: D8/§4.4: the two merge-gate.md reads pinned verbatim with `base_path` built from `baseRefName`; each output and exit status recorded; empty protection read = pass; a 403 from either read stops and goes to the architect (`branches/main/protection` 403 is not one of the reads).

findings.finding: 25. Both `E2E` lines are approval-blocking and must each carry a link, which is easy to miss on a docs-only PR whose 'surface' is a file read.
findings.answer: D9/D17/§3: both `E2E` lines carry the blob link at the judged SHA and one named negative control per criterion; approval refused without them; the implementer's proof re-read at the retro head R (D20).

findings.finding: 26. The plan must state the docs-only consequences with their sources, or a reviewer will look for a `Thermo` line and a tester for a test suite.
findings.answer: D14: no ce-simplify-code pass, no thermonuclear pair, no Thermo line (pr-body.md, merge-gate.md), no test file; the tester's duty is independent re-reads of served bytes with negative controls and reading CI, never rerunning it.

findings.finding: 27. Retro's PR-body derivation steps and the bot-thread procedure both need a stated no-op/ procedure for this repository, or retro will stall on step 1.
findings.answer: D17/§4.1 step 8/§4.5: retro's body derivation is a no-op (AGENTS.md, PR template, docs/ all 404); retro updates only lines its commits make stale; bot threads get one disposition reply each and implementer-only resolution via review-threads.md, no marker byte changes.

findings.finding: 28. The `.fail-me` cure must be read at the right ref: the `gate` job evaluates the file after `actions/checkout@v4`, which for a `pull_request` event checks out the merge ref, not the branch head.
findings.answer: §6.2: read `.fail-me` at the branch head and on `main` first (gate runs after actions/checkout@v4 on the pull_request merge ref); cure is a deletion-only commit on the branch, never `gh run rerun`; post-cure four green check-runs at the new code head; one on `main` goes to the architect.

findings.finding: 29. P says the change reaches `main` 'through one pull request', and nothing in the plan forbids a replacement PR or bookmark if a push is refused.
findings.answer: D22/§6.3: one PR from legion/LEGSMOKE-914; a refused push is reported with its output, never forced, never a new bookmark or second PR.

findings.finding: 30. P's post-merge clause ('the file read from `main` … holds the lines the Acceptance section describes for the review's outcome') has no stated arm-selector after the merge, when the review comments are the only remaining evidence of which arm applied.
findings.answer: D13/§4.6: the post-merge read recomputes RV and K on the closed pull request and records K beside the byte check.

findings.finding: 31. Nothing in the Acceptance covers CI on `main` after the merge, so a role could wait on a gate the spec never asked for.
findings.answer: End of §1: `main`'s own push runs after the merge are not an acceptance gate; post-merge evidence is the contents read plus the merge commit's file list.
